name: Porto Pollo
notes: Kite zone on the Porto Liscia (west) side of the Isola dei Gabbiani isthmus; the Porto Pollo bay itself is windsurf only (Capitaneria La Maddalena order 38/2016: no kites in the bay from Easter Sunday to 10 Nov; Porto Liscia has a buoyed kite corridor; beyond 200 m from shore otherwise). Mistral (W–NW) and libeccio; schools on site.

name: Punta Trettu
notes: Flat lagoon-like water inside a metre deep for hundreds of metres, beside Sant'Antioco: the beginner spot of Sardinia. Mistral (NW) and scirocco (SE), thermal in summer. Launch only from the kite beach (small entry fee in season); algae on the bottom. Also: Porto Botte (flat bay).

name: Porto Botte
notes: Very shallow bay with standing depth far out: flat water, good for learning. Mistral (NW) works best.

name: Cagliari – Poetto
notes: Long city beach; works with scirocco / SE and the summer sea breeze. Summer: no launch corridor and crowded; Hyperisland says the Comune closes it 15 Jun–15 Sep (not an official text, so no ban encoded); kiters move to Petrol Beach or Punta Trettu. Rideable outside that.

name: San Teodoro – La Cinta
notes: Long sandbar beach; works with levante / scirocco (onshore). Summer: kite corridor only.

name: Putzu Idu
notes: Sinis peninsula; mistral (NW) side-shore, chop to small waves. Schools on site. Also: Capo Mannu next door (rocky, big waves, experts only).

name: Lo Stagnone (Marsala)
notes: Shallow flat-water lagoon, standing almost everywhere; many schools. Thermal / scirocco / mistral all work. Keep clear of swimming areas. The lagoon is inside the Stagnone nature reserve: kiting is contested (Legambiente says the reserve rules ban it, Nov 2026; schools operate under harbour-office ordinance 1/2019, which limits sailing to about 200 m inside the reserve). No official ban text found: ask your school or the Marsala harbour office.

name: Mazara del Vallo – Capo Feto
notes: Wild beach next to the Capo Feto nature reserve; flat water inside the reef with W–NW, chop further out. Steady NW thermal (16–19 kn) in summer, also works with W and SE. North wind (tramontana) is offshore and gusty: dangerous. Sandy, bumpy access track. Kite school on site (Kitesurf Mazara, IKO).

name: Santa Maria del Focallo
notes: Long sandy beach on the south-east coast (Ispica): open sea without heavy waves, a beginner-friendly spot. Best wind W thermal April to October. A kite zone is marked off from June to September: keep about 200 m from the shore. Schools on the beach (Floripa, Sicily Kite School). Also: Pozzallo and Marina di Ragusa along the same coast.

name: Gizzeria – Hang Loose Beach
notes: Very reliable thermal (W–NW) from spring to autumn, funnelled across the narrowest point of Italy. Large kite beach with schools (Hang Loose Beach, open 1 April to 30 September).

name: Porto Cesareo – Torre Lapillo
notes: Ionian coast, the best-known Salento spot: works with S to WNW winds and the summer sea breeze. Waves over a reef on the north side, flat water in the Strea lagoon to the south. Schools on site. Summer bathing season: check the local rules, no official kite-zone text found.

name: Torre Canne
notes: Adriatic beach; maestrale (NW) and N-NE winds, flat to choppy. Kite school on site (Scuola Kitesurf Puglia, since 2011). Summer bathing season: check the local rules, no official kite-zone text found.

name: Margherita di Savoia
notes: Long shallow Adriatic beach; maestrale (NW) side-shore and thermal. Chop and small waves, wide launch area. Schools on site (Wind People at Lido Valerio, Garganosurf).

name: Rosolina Mare
notes: Adriatic beach near the Po delta; bora (NE) and scirocco onshore. Summer: kite corridor only.

name: Lago di Garda – Campione
notes: Thermal winds: Pelèr (N) in the morning, Ora (S) in the afternoon. Kiting via the local kite centre (boat launch). Also: Malcesine / Navene on the east shore (kite school with boat; Garda kiting regulated by zones and times).

name: Lago di Santa Croce
notes: Small lake in the Alpago; reliable afternoon thermal in summer, Bora-type north wind in the morning. Kite schools on site.

name: Lago di Resia (Reschensee)
notes: High-altitude reservoir (about 1,500 m) with a reliable valley wind in summer; cold water, full wetsuit. Kite schools at Graun / Reschen.

name: Talamone
notes: Bay north of the Argentario; libeccio (SW) and W thermal, flat to choppy. Schools on site.

Rena Majore
notes: Large sandy beach on the north coast: NW wind strongest, choppy to small waves; rocks on both sides and a tricky entry. Crowded with swimmers in summer.

region: WHE-169 (2026-11-14). Sources per row in docs/validation/it-sardegna.md

name: Cagliari – Petrol Beach
notes: The summer kite spot of the Gulf of Cagliari (La Maddalena Spiaggia, Capoterra): thermal SW-S wind on hot days, chop, launch corridor and a school on site. Poetto is closed to kites in summer.

name: La Caletta (Siniscola)
notes: East coast: SE thermal late spring to late summer, plus east winds; kite zone with launch corridor and two schools (Kitesurf La Caletta and Active Kite).

name: Villasimius – Campulongu
notes: Winter spot (Oct–May): W-SW wind at Campulongu, rocks here and there, narrow beach; Porto Giunco next door works with NE. In high season only with a lift service (Sardegna Turismo).

name: Capo Mannu
notes: Big wave spot on the Sinis cape: strong mistral (NW) after a few days of wind, shared with surfers, no sandy exit. Experts only. School: Capo Mannu Kite School.

name: Porto Pino
notes: South-west dune beach: mistral side-off and libeccio, gusty near the dunes. Summer: no open kiting (swimmers); the school at Lido Oasi Azzurra has an authorised zone for its guests (1 Jun–30 Sep).

name: Chia
notes: South coast sand beaches: SE and NW work, waves and chop. Crowded June–September, no kite zone, so a lift or boat is needed in summer; school on site.

name: Vignola Mare
notes: Far north: the steadiest wind on the north shore (W or E–NE); small kite area, rocks both sides, crowded July–August (keep 100 m from swimmers). Vignola Sports school; Blue Zone courses suspended.

name: Valledoria – La Foce
notes: River mouth lagoon (flat) with chop and waves at sea; W best then NE, thermal 14–25 kn in summer. Safe entry and exit; school and shop on site.

name: Funtana Meiga
notes: Sinis beach used when Capo Mannu is too big: mistral above about 25–30 kn. Wave spot, experienced riders; no school found.

name: Kiteloop
Punta Pellaro
notes: Sandy spit at the southern tip of Reggio Calabria on the Strait of Messina: north to NNW wind, steadier from spring to summer with the thermal (May to August strongest). Current of 1-2 knots, typical of the strait. Several schools on site.

Vieste – Spiaggia Lunga (Scialmarino)
notes: Long beach on the north side of Gargano, 5 km from Vieste (also called Scialmarino): north and east winds, thermal 10-15 knots May to September. Intermediate level. Crowded in summer, rocks at both ends, possible current. Schools: Gargano Kitesurf, SurfConcept.

name: San Foca
notes: Adriatic coast of Salento: best with north winds (tramontana, grecale), which also give chop for freestyle. Works October to May as well as summer. Several schools between San Foca and Torre dell'Orso.

Alimini
notes: Adriatic beach north of Otranto: north wind, intermediate to advanced. School AK at the Voi Alimini resort (also Frassanito next door, advanced, north wind can pass 20 knots).

Apani
notes: Sandy beach with shallow water north of Brindisi: north and north-east winds (tramontana, maestrale). Intermediate level, open all year. No school based on the beach.

name: Kite Jungle and Breeza guides; experts only
Capo Peloro (Torre Faro)
notes: North-east tip of Sicily on the Strait of Messina, at Il Pilone and Punta del Faro: strong scirocco (to 40 knots) and the strait wind. Stony beach, deep water close in and a strong current: experienced riders only, go with someone who knows it. No school on the spot.

name: IKO
locate: SurfTribe spot page; summer use unclear

name: Gallipoli – Lido Pizzo
notes: Ionian coast near Gallipoli: NW to SW winds per the school (the kite pitch itself faces north), fine sand, easy entry. School Salento Coast Ovest teaches here, moving to Torre San Giovanni in summer. One older page says the bay is off-limits to kites from June to September: ask the school.

region: WHE-170 — schools Crazykiter and Gargano Lake Kite at Acquarotta
name: Let's Kite spot guide
Marina di Lesina – Acquarotta
notes: Adriatic beach at the mouth of Lake Lesina: sea side with waves in north wind, intermediate, April to September. The lake behind is flat, shallow and kite-school access only (beginners).
